story.thread: Winners fix ONE persistent spatial substrate and never let it go quiet, then carry ONE reversible motion vocabulary over it hero-to-footer. The substrate is either a living WebGL ground (Igloo's real-time ice scene; OceanX's ocean; Iventions' lighting rig) OR, in the no-3D register, an authored atmosphere of organic clip-path geometry (Cyd's periwinkle #8082F8 blob shapes recurring on every tile + a wordmark marquee overflowing and drifting under scroll). The reversible vocabulary layered on it is a single easing family (illustrative Cyd values, exact numerics unverified: --default-ease cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1) ease-out-quart, --bouncy-ease cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1)), one radius language, one accent, one bespoke display face, and one signature text move: a variable-font optical-axis scroll-morph driven by native animation-timeline (a real, executable technique — font-variation-settings interpolated across a scroll view-range; Cyd's specific axis and amplitudes are unverified, any registered axis such as weight or optical-size executes it). Cohesion is the shared substrate + the one easing family; VARIETY is the per-class mechanism — accent-displacement for buttons, an underline scaleX draw for links, a border-radius-morph + crossfade for figures, spotlight-dim for index rows, silence or same-family glass for nav. The AI failure is the inverse: one pale-fill hover copied onto every class over an ad-hoc palette, and a section that goes flat/static after the hero.
story.copy: One long intro sentence, then noun-phrase labels — the substrate carries the mood, the words name the nouns. Person tracks subject: product/company -> first-person-plural manifesto (Igloo names its noun and its frontier: 'create the largest onchain community, driving the consumer crypto revolution', no button follows); studio -> third-person, process-as-offer (no verified corpus quote this run — the prior Obys/Aristide example is out-of-window/uncorroborated, see unverified); solo -> first person + availability-as-fact (Cyd: 'Available October 2026' / 'Have a project in mind?' — availability stated, contact asked). Warm verbs, never transactional; terminal marks (//) in the engine register, slash-indexing in portfolios; refuses hype, pricing, feature-lists, exclamation marks. Imitate the specificity — the named place, the count, the refusal — never the wording.

spectacle_model.hero: The first viewport commits the SPATIAL SUBSTRATE, never a filled CTA (shared corpus law — the call is a scroll cue or an email link). Two register-branches: (1) WebGL register — the fold IS the live scene. Igloo's intro shader flows straight into the outdoor scene with in-engine HUD corners (wordmark, mission line, scroll cue, sound toggle, node-graph) from frame ~0 BECAUSE it is a single real-time scene (verified, no loader). Asset-heavy Three.js sites do NOT start at frame ~0: OceanX enters via a designed 'Intro Transition WebGL' (verified tag), Minh Pham / Iventions load models/textures behind a designed preload/enter-gate — the 'no loader boundary' is Igloo-specific, NOT an archetype law (see the webgl-preload-gate gap). (2) Warm-organic register — a composed organic fold: Cyd's repeating variable-font wordmark strip over a real portrait mounted on a periwinkle (#8082F8) clip-path blob, a badge sticker scale-in (.4s @.2s bouncy) and a second sticker scroll-retimed via animation-timeline (exact ranges unverified). Either branch must be ALIVE at rest once entered (drifting orbs / breathing idle / a running shader) — a motion-dead, pointer-dead spatial hero is this archetype's first-impression defect.
continuation: Igloo (winner-verified): the WebGL substrate carries every seam — ice-block sections are separated by chromatic-aberration + tech-displacement + frost transitions (the substrate IS the transition), the links section is an interactive particle simulation (colour-by-speed, glow on shape-shift, sound-synced), and the close is a standard DOM footer with nav/links (NOT an in-engine sign-off — refuted this run). Peak lands LATE at the particle sim; between inputs the scene drifts. Zero silence, the hero is not the peak.

Cyd (winner-verified): after the fold peak, the vocabulary runs unbroken — the variable-font optical-axis morph rides animation-timeline across the page (a display heading morphs its axis across its scroll entry-range; the footer wordmark runs the axis on its own timeline — exact axis/values unverified), the wordmark marquee overflows the viewport and drifts under scroll, per-block entrances fire once, and the idle band breathes (a folder image translate on a slow loop, a wordmark ticker). The morph-tile grid carries the organic geometry; the footer wordmark morph is the quiet second peak.

OceanX (verified): documentary pacing on a HORIZONTAL axis — each chapter peaks then releases while a diegetic exploration ship guides a free-scroll WebGL timeline; the WebGL ocean substrate and its depth-layering never stop moving beneath the copy, so the 'release' beats are still driven, not static.

Iventions / Minh Pham (verified): the lighting rig runs continuously; GSAP paces one spotlit project reveal after another as a guided walk-through — the depth/lighting is the sustained thread, reveals escalate exhibit by exhibit, the 3D never parks.

Exo Ape / Fluid Glass (verified): the restrained end — mask-wipe transitions on scroll keep the surface moving between sections; the underline scaleX draw and custom lerp scroll thread the whole read even where the grade is minimal.
evidence: Igloo: the single WebGL substrate spans frame-one intro shader -> ice-block sections (each seam a frost/chromatic-aberration/displacement transition) -> the interactive particle-simulation links section — the dominant PEAK lands LATE at the particle sim, the hero is not the climax, and there is no silent section between them. This is the reference's own Animations/Transitions 9.60 centerpiece (R2 CONFIRMED this run) and it directly contradicts 'one wow at the hero then quiet'.

Cyd: peaks are genuinely CAPPED at one dominant (the fold) plus a quiet second (the footer wordmark morph) — but the substrate vocabulary (organic clip-path geometry + variable-font axis scroll-morph + marquee drift + idle breathing) is MANDATORY every section, never multiplied into more peaks. This is the warm-organic proof that continuation is ambient/reversible, not a stack of spectacles.

OceanX: documentary pacing where 'intensity peaks and releases' is a chaptered multi-rise over one continuous ocean substrate on a horizontal axis — neither one-peak-then-silence nor immersive's sustained multi-peak, but a rhythm of rises above a never-static ground.

Iventions/Minh Pham: the spotlit lighting rig is the continuation; the win is explicitly 'WebGL used for atmosphere instead of spectacle' — a persistent driven ground with no loud peak at all, refuting the idea that the archetype needs a hero wow to hold.

Across the corpus the substrate is the identity: a section that goes flat/static/pointer-dead after the hero is the archetype's defining defect, because spatial-organic's whole premise is CONTINUOUS depth, not a single dimensional moment.
spectacle_model.recommended_law: For spatial-organic, keep 'peaks are capped' but make the continuation MANDATORY and register the late-peak: ship a PERSISTENT SPATIAL SUBSTRATE spanning hero->footer — a living ground (a WebGL scene, an ambient OKLCH orb field, or procedural noise) plus a reversible motion vocabulary (organic clip-path geometry, a variable-font optical-axis scroll-morph, and a named idle band) — and CAP the amplitude peaks at ONE dominant plus an optional quiet second at the footer. The dominant peak is NOT required to sit at the hero: the hero commits the SUBSTRATE, and the peak may land late (Igloo's particle sim, a documentary's deepest chapter, or — unverified — a type-index's on-click route morph). The failure to forbid is SILENCE: a section where the substrate goes static or the page reads flat/rectangular/pointer-dead is 'no depth', the defect. Peaks are scarce; the substrate is not optional; a flat section is the sin. (Distinct from immersive, where peaks may multiply — here the warm-organic register genuinely caps peaks and lets the continuation stay ambient.)

Every section must keep the substrate driven — a flat, rectangular, pointer-dead, motion-silent section is illegal here (the silence defect). Prefer soft clip-path curved section edges over rectangular boundaries (the anti-grid flow). Rotate section shapes against the previous stamp; never re-sequence a winner's ordering to taste.

algorithm.decide: The momentum map — the substrate mechanic + one capped peak (+ optional footer second) + the between-input idle band + an optional velocity channel.
algorithm.rule: Assign the SUBSTRATE: what runs every section (WebGL scene drift / ambient orb drift 15-25s cycles / procedural noise) plus the reversible vocabulary (VF axis scroll-morph, wordmark marquee drift, clip-path geometry, native animation-timeline reveals firing once). Fill BETWEEN inputs with a named idle band (orb drift + folder/image breathing + a wordmark ticker) so the page breathes at rest. Optionally add a SCROLL-VELOCITY channel on the smooth-scroll (Lenis/lerp) foundation: map instantaneous scroll speed to a transform on scrolling media (skew/scale/RGB-split proportional to velocity, damped to rest on stop) — the velocity register, distinct from time-driven idle drift and fire-once reveals. Verdict test: if any section's base is static and only a decorative overlay moves, the substrate was not built — fix before proceeding.

algorithm.decide: Per-element interaction states — the differentiated hover/tap/focus per element class.
algorithm.rule: Apply the element_states canon: CTA = accent-displacement push (translate + hard offset shadow in the accent on the opposite side) or a committed same-family/80% fill for the single primary, NEVER a pale tint. Link = underline scaleX draw (or 10% wash + 1px lift + arrow nudge for utility links) — the accent line belongs on links, never as nav chrome. Figure = border-radius morph + crossfade (geometry carries it, no accent) or focus-defocus in the spotlit register. Index row = spotlight-dim (accent rule + surfaced meta, siblings to ~45%). Heading = NO pointer hover — the VF optical-axis scroll-morph + a fire-once masked reveal carry it. Nav = underline-draw + transparent->same-family glass or a borderless same-cream bar, NEVER an accent border-bottom, NEVER a fill (OR a diegetic path in the WebGL register). The displacement/draw/morph is the response; any tint/wash is set-dressing that alone fails the pale-hover gate. Run 4-5 distinct interaction channels (per-class states, VF display effect, cursor-as-choice, idle band, scroll texture).

algorithm.rule: Pointer classes go DORMANT on touch (pointer-parallax, conic-border-shine, focus-defocus, magnetic, custom follower, liquid-glass-refraction); depth comes from SCROLL — native CSS animation-timeline reveals and the VF axis morph both run on touch, plus clip-path reveals. Horizontal-Layout chains convert to native horizontal swipe-snap on touch rather than a pinned scrub; a diegetic ship/path nav degrades to an anchored nav + progress indicator. Reconsider the WebGL scene, don't drop it: lower poly, fewer orbs, progressive quality, static frame under low-power. Glass keeps its OPAQUE fallback and backdrop-filter stays ONLY on fixed/sticky elements (never on scrolling containers — the perf lock). Press-class controls answer the tap with a 90-160ms flash floor (the displacement/fill IS the tap answer). Galleries -> swipe-snap-gallery riding OS momentum with tap-to-enlarge. No follower cursor. Reduced-motion freezes the scene to a legible frame and swaps scrubbed media to a poster.

cta.hover: Accent-displacement push: the base surface barely moves, the button translates a few px and a hard, UN-blurred offset shadow in the accent appears on the OPPOSITE side (a card lifting off a colored underlayer) — Cyd .button:hover translate(-2px,2px), box-shadow -1px 1px 0 accent, background color-mix(ground 95%, accent 5%) (the 5% tint is set-dressing), 64px pill, bouncy-ease (exact values unverified). For the SINGLE primary submit per view, swap to a committed same-family fill (color-mix(accent 80%, ground)) or a full-token flood (fill-invert-cta). NEVER a pale pastel tint — a tint-only state with no geometry move fails the pale-hover gate.
cta.tap: The displacement/fill IS the tap answer — :active collapses the offset back to translate(0,0) / shadow 0, 90-160ms; on touch the pointer-displacement is dormant so :active must carry it.
cta.focus: Same displacement + offset shadow on :focus-visible, plus a visible ring — the hover state reachable by keyboard.

link.hover: Underline draw — a pseudo-element scaling scaleX 0->1 (NOT a text-decoration toggle): Exo Ape runs one :hover::after transform:scaleX(1) across nav, list, footer AND body links, colour shifting to a light-grey. For inline/utility links, a 10% accent wash + a 1px lift + a diagonal arrow shove: Cyd .platform-link:hover background color-mix(accent, transparent 90%), translateY(-1px), arrow child translate(2px,-2px). The draw/lift/shove is the response; the wash is set-dressing (wash alone fails the pale gate). The accent line lives on links, never as nav chrome.
link.tap: Underline present / arrow settled on :active (90-160ms flash).

figure.hover: Border-radius morph + crossfade: the tile's radius animates rounder to --hover-radius while a resting circle/graphic crossfades (opacity 1->0) to the full image (0->1) and the caption slides up — Cyd .work-thumb:hover, opacity/border-radius timing on the signature ease (exact durations unverified). No accent — the ORGANIC GEOMETRY carries it (organic-shape-native, cheaper than a WebGL displacement). In the spotlit register the hovered figure sharpens while siblings blur+dim (focus-defocus). Contained zoom 1.1 is the fallback, never a 1.02-1.03 twitch.
figure.tap: The morphed/colored state on tap, or tap-to-enlarge (the swipe-snap-gallery Mobile Excellence line); the resting caption is the complete rest look.
figure.focus: Same on :focus-within — the full image / caption reachable under keyboard and touch.

index_row.hover: Spotlight-dim — the hovered row lights (accent rule + surfaced metadata) while siblings dim to ~45% (index-row-hover); :has() dims the unhovered siblings. In the type-index register (unverified pattern) the giant-type row over the WebGL ground carries the hover; the row is the page.
index_row.tap: Row expands or navigates; the surfaced metadata hover reveals is present in the resting DOM (reachable under touch).
index_row.focus: Accent rule + surfaced meta on :focus-within, siblings dim — same spotlight, keyboard-driven.

heading.hover: NONE by pointer — winner-verified: there is no heading, prose, or number hover anywhere in the read corpus. Text motion rides SCROLL and TIME, not the pointer: a variable-font optical-axis scroll-morph via native animation-timeline (font-variation-settings interpolated across a scroll view-range — a real, executable technique confirmed this run via Codrops/Carmen Ansio; Cyd's specific 'ytuc' axis at 80/100/0 is unverified and physically implausible — YTUC is 'Parametric Uppercase Height', a font-unit-height axis — so use a registered axis such as weight or optical-size). Per-line/char masked reveal fires ONCE on scroll-in. Hover-on-text stays link-scoped only.
heading.tap: None as a hover analog — the scroll/time morph is device-agnostic (native animation-timeline runs on touch).
heading.focus: None as a hover analog; clean accessible name via aria-label when the mark is split for the reveal.

nav.hover: REGISTER SPLIT: the conventional top bar below is the warm-organic/DOM register's nav. In the WebGL nature/engine register the primary nav may be DIEGETIC instead of a bar — a vehicle/map/scrubbable path the visit moves through (OceanX's exploration ship guiding a free-scroll timeline, Awwwards-tagged 'Unusual Navigation'/'Horizontal Layout'; Fluid Glass Awwwards-tagged 'Unusual Navigation') — see the diegetic-nav gap; it replaces the bar, not decorates it. Conventional bar: per-link underline-draw (the same scaleX draw as body links) — NEVER a fill, never an accent border-bottom. The bar itself: transparent over the hero, then a low-alpha SAME-FAMILY tint + backdrop-filter:blur() once content scrolls under (Arc/Granola style-anchors), OR a solid same-cream sticky bar, borderless (Cyd #FFF5EE, border-bottom:none). The only permitted line is a same-family hairline (Granola #E3E3E3), never a contrasting accent bar.
nav.tap: Menu toggle answers the tap; link taps present the underline. A diegetic nav degrades to an anchored nav + progress indicator on touch.
nav.focus: Underline draw + visible ring; reveals on scroll-up / hides on scroll-down and stays keyboard-reachable.

cursor.hover: A CHOICE, not a reflex. Custom DOM follower on image/scene-forward builds (Exo Ape and Granola carry a follower element); a deliberate SYSTEM cursor on a text/editorial build (Cyd, an SOTD winner, ships NO follower and leans on the button displacement + View Transitions). In the WebGL register the pointer drives the ground (Igloo's particle sim responds; a fluid mouse-ripple is the medium's pointer layer). Magnetic pull is JS-driven and unverified on any corpus site — optional, never a default.
cursor.tap: Follower + all pointer classes go native/dormant on touch; the tap is answered by the press-class element, not the cursor.
cursor.focus: N/A — pointer-only; keyboard users get the finished/revealed state without the pointer choreography.

mobile_answer: Pointer-driven classes go DORMANT on touch (pointer-parallax, conic-border-shine, focus-defocus, magnetic-cursor, the DOM follower, liquid-glass-refraction) — on mobile the depth comes from SCROLL: the native CSS animation-timeline reveals and the variable-font optical-axis morph both run on touch, plus clip-path reveals, so the archetype keeps its identity without the pointer. Horizontal-Layout chains (OceanX, Fluid Glass) convert to native horizontal swipe-snap on touch rather than a pinned scrub; a diegetic ship/path nav degrades to an anchored nav + progress indicator. The WebGL substrate is reconsidered not dropped (lower poly, fewer orbs, progressive quality low->high, static frame under low-power). Glass keeps its OPAQUE fallback and backdrop-filter stays ONLY on fixed/sticky surfaces — applying it to a scrolling container triggers continuous GPU repaints and collapses mobile frame rate (the reference's Performance lock); ambient orbs sit on fixed pointer-events:none layers, never on scrolling ones. Press-class controls answer the tap with a 90-160ms flash floor (the displacement/fill is the tap answer, since pointer-displacement is dormant). Galleries become swipe-snap-gallery tracks riding OS momentum with tap-to-enlarge (the scored Mobile Excellence line). No follower cursor. prefers-reduced-motion freezes the scene/orbs to a legible frame and swaps scrubbed media to a poster; Cyd ships its whole motion set on View Transitions + native animation-timeline, mobile-safe by construction.

Slots: wordmark-strip, utility-row, portrait(figure-on-clip-path), role-h1, badge x2. No filled fold CTA — a scroll cue or email link only. The recipe studio-reel-cyd already flags MISSING:marquee-hero; hero-masthead cannot express the marquee strip, the clip-path portrait mount, or the scroll-retimed sticker.

gaps.mechanic: The archetype's signature text move and its cheapest continuation channel, and NOTHING in the manifest executes it. Spec: bind a variable-font axis to an element's scroll view-range via native animation-timeline — a display heading rides animation-timeline:--range morphing font-variation-settings across animation-range: entry X entry Y, and the footer wordmark runs the axis on its own --footer timeline; reversible by construction, off the main thread, guaranteed 60fps. Use a REGISTERED axis (weight 'wght' or optical-size 'opsz') — Cyd's cited 'ytuc' axis at 80/100/0 is unverified and physically implausible (YTUC = 'Parametric Uppercase Height', a font-unit-height axis, documented range e.g. 528-760, not 80/0). Degrades to the static authored axis with no timeline and under prefers-reduced-motion (the pre-animation state lives only inside the @supports(animation-timeline) guard). kinetic-reveal (line mask), char-assemble (per-char), text-emphasis-fill (word brighten) and semantic-accent (term color) are ALL discrete/opacity effects — none animate a font-variation-settings axis on scroll.

gaps.mechanic: The DNA-core spatial substrate for the no-WebGL register, currently only faked by the generic ambient-idle or the heavier shader-surface. Spec: a FIXED, pointer-events:none layer of 2-3 large-radius OKLCH radial-gradient orbs at low opacity (0.15-0.25), filter:blur(~80px), each drifting on a 15-25s ease-in-out alternate cycle (translate a few vw + scale 1->1.1); compositor-only (transform/opacity), paused off-screen and on hidden tabs, static frame under prefers-reduced-motion. The cheap, WebGL-free living ground the momentum model needs for the warm/dark-glass registers — ambient-idle opts single elements into glow/float but cannot compose the drifting multi-orb atmosphere behind glass, and shader-surface requires a WebGL/canvas path.

The organic-shape work grid whose hover IS the archetype's figure signature. Spec: a grid of tiles that each pair a border-radius morph with a crossfade — on hover/focus-within the .img-container radius animates rounder to --hover-radius while a resting circle/graphic overlay crossfades (opacity 1->0) to the full image (0->1) and the caption title slides up (translateY(0)); no accent, the geometry carries it. figure-hover (in card-list/feature-card-grid) does a contained zoom-to-1.1 + companion cue — a DIFFERENT mechanic; the recipe studio-reel-cyd flags MISSING:morph-tile-grid because neither the radius-morph nor the circle->full crossfade exists today.

The anti-grid flow boundary — the DNA says 'shapes flow rather than snap to grids; soft clip-path curves replace rectangular sections', yet every current form is a rectangle. Spec: a section-wrapper utility carrying a clip-path ellipse/blob top and/or bottom edge (variants: clip-path: ellipse(80% 100% at 50% 0%) etc.), optionally with an offset shadow riding the curved edge in the accent (Cyd's footer clip-path edge + periwinkle #8082F8 offset shadow); pure CSS, no motion of its own, degrades to a straight edge with no clip-path support. No component or form owns organic section clipping today — clip-reveal is a MEDIA uncover, not a section boundary.

The macrostructure the playbook's vertical-only grammar omits. Both OceanX 2025 and Fluid Glass carry the Awwwards 'Horizontal Layout' tag (verified on their own Awwwards pages this run). Spec: a pinned full-viewport section whose inner track translates HORIZONTALLY (transform:translateX) as vertical scroll distance is consumed (GSAP ScrollTrigger pin+scrub or a scroll-driven timeline); the WebGL/organic substrate rides the horizontal axis, section seams become horizontal wipes, and progress reads as lateral travel. On touch it degrades to native horizontal swipe-snap. No form or step encoded a horizontal chain before this revision — step-3 macrostructure and step-4 momentum assumed vertical advance (now amended).

Spatial/diegetic primary navigation for the WebGL nature/engine register, absent from the nav element_state's conventional-top-bar default. Spec: the visit is steered by an in-world object the user moves along a path rather than a top bar — OceanX embeds an exploration ship that guides a free-scroll timeline (forwards or backwards at any point; verified via Awwwards + case study, Awwwards-tagged 'Unusual Navigation'/'Horizontal Layout'), Fluid Glass is Awwwards-tagged 'Unusual Navigation'. Slots: a moving avatar/vehicle, a scrubbable path/timeline, milestone markers, a wayfinding minimap. Degrades to a conventional anchored nav + progress indicator on touch/reduced-motion. For an archetype whose premise is 'the visit moves THROUGH a scene', a diegetic nav is a structural component, not a detail.

A designed preload/enter sequence for asset-heavy WebGL, and the correction to the over-generalized 'no loader' law. Igloo flows from frame ~0 only because it is a SINGLE real-time scene (verified); the multi-asset Three.js winners load models/textures and cannot start at frame ~0 — OceanX's own Awwwards feature names an 'Intro Transition WebGL' (verified this run). Spec: a branded progress/enter gate that (1) tracks real asset-load progress, (2) resolves into the scene via a designed transition rather than a hard cut, (3) doubles as the first spectacle beat. The prior playbook FORBADE a loader by law for all WebGL registers; it is now Igloo-specific and the enter-gate is the heavy-3D default. Confidence medium — the multi-asset nature and the named intro transition are verified, a specific loader frame is not.

The velocity-driven continuation channel missing from the ambient-only momentum map. Velocity is already a verified live input: Igloo's particles 'change colour based on their speed' (verified case study). Spec: on the smooth-scroll (Lenis/lerp) foundation, map instantaneous scroll velocity to a transform on scrolling media — skewY/scaleY, a slight scale, or an RGB-split proportional to speed, damped back to rest on stop; compositor-only, capped amplitude, disabled under reduced-motion. Distinct from idle drift (time-driven) and fire-once reveals — this is the scroll-speed register. step-4's momentum map covered only idle + reveals + a smooth-scroll foundation (now amended). Confidence medium — Igloo's speed-as-input is verified; the specific skew mechanic is the GSAP/Lenis pattern, not pinned to a corpus screenshot.

The WebGL-register hero: monospace HUD corners mounted over a live full-viewport scene from frame ~0. Spec (WebGL-delegated): a fold form whose slots are HUD chrome — wordmark, mission line, scroll cue, sound toggle, and a live node-graph — positioned at the viewport corners over a shader-surface/webgl-scene ground; no CTA, the fold IS the scene, the intro flows in with no loader boundary for a single real-time scene; text effects (glitch/scramble) done in-shader (SDF offset) rather than DOM.
